feedback.problem:
Consider the curve defined parametrically as 

$$
x=2{e}^{5t},\,y=5{e}^{2t},\,t\in [0,1].
$$

What integral gives the surface area generated when this curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis?
feedback.worked_solution:
We can find the surface area generated when a curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis using the formula

$$
S=\int 2\pi x\,\text{d}s.
$$

Since our curve is given in parametric form, we have

$$
\text{d}s=\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Therefore, we will use

$$
S=2\pi {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}x\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

We are told that the limits of integration are from ${t}_{1}=0$ to ${t}_{2}=1.$ 

Computing the derivatives, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{e}^{5t})=10{e}^{5t} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5{e}^{2t})=10{e}^{2t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =2\pi {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}x\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}2{e}^{5t}\sqrt{{(10{e}^{5t})}^{2}+{(10{e}^{2t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =4\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{5t}\sqrt{100{e}^{10t}+100{e}^{4t}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =4\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{5t}\sqrt{100{e}^{4t}({e}^{6t}+1)}\,\text{d}t \\  & =4\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{5t}\cdot \sqrt{100{e}^{4t}}\cdot \sqrt{{e}^{6t}+1}\,\text{d}t \\  & =4\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{5t}\cdot 10{e}^{2t}\cdot \sqrt{{e}^{6t}+1}\,\text{d}t \\  & =40\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{7t}\sqrt{{e}^{6t}+1}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$
